# Snapblade diagrams: instructions for AI agents

Snapblade is a browser editor for box-and-line diagrams (architecture, systems, data flows) and sequence diagrams: https://mmunchinski.github.io/snapblade/
You write a diagram as JSON. The user saves your answer as a file ending in `.snapblade` (or `.json`) and opens it in Snapblade (File > Open, or drop it on the canvas).

In a box diagram you decide what the shapes are and where they go. Snapblade draws the connectors itself: it picks the sides, spaces the anchor points, routes right-angled lines around the shapes and places the labels. So give every shape a sensible position and size, and leave the connector details on automatic. A sequence diagram has no positions at all: you list the participants and the messages in order, and Snapblade lays it out (see Sequence diagrams). One file can also hold several diagrams as tabs (see the last section).

These instructions are generated from the app's own rules, so they always match the current version.

## What to output

One JSON object and nothing else (no comments, no trailing commas), in a single json code block. Tell the user to save it as `<name>.snapblade` and open it in Snapblade.

    {"format": "snapblade", "version": 1, "diagram": {"nodes": [...], "edges": [...], "settings": {...}, "title": {...}, "legend": {...}}}

That is a box diagram, where only `nodes` and `edges` are required. A sequence diagram puts `"type": "sequence"`, `parts` and `rows` in `diagram` instead of `nodes` and `edges`. For several diagrams in one file, use version 2 with a `pages` list. Anything missing gets its default. Anything not described here, or not one of the listed values, is dropped or reset to its default when the file is opened.

## Coordinates (box diagrams)

Pixels. `x` grows to the right and `y` grows downward; `x` and `y` are a shape's top-left corner. Positions must be within -1000000 to 1000000, sizes from 1 to 100000. Use multiples of 10.

## Shapes (`nodes`)

    {"id": "orders", "kind": "box", "label": "Orders API", "x": 520, "y": 140, "w": 160, "h": 60, "parent": null}

- `id` (required): letters, digits, `_` or `-`, 1 to 64 characters, unique among shapes. Connectors and children refer to shapes by id.
- `kind`: "box" or "group". A `"group"` is a container: it holds other shapes and shows its label as a header. Default `"box"`.
- `label`: the text. `\n` starts a new line. Default empty.
- `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`: position and size. Defaults 0, 0, 120 and 60.
- `parent`: the id of the container this shape is inside, or `null` (the default) for the canvas. It must be a `"group"`.
- `style`: colors and line pattern; see Styles. Optional.

Containers (`"kind": "group"`) also have:

- `layout`: "free", "row" or "column". `"free"` (default): children sit at their own `x` and `y`, and the container grows to keep them inside (it never shrinks). `"row"` and `"column"`: children are stacked left to right or top to bottom, in the order they appear in `nodes`, `gap` apart; their `x` and `y` are ignored (write 0), and so are the container's `w` and `h`: it sizes itself to fit. Only its own `x` and `y` matter. The first child's top-left corner lands at the container's `x + pad`, `y + 30 + pad`; a column is as wide as its widest child plus `2 × pad` (at least 140), a row as tall as its tallest child plus `30 + 2 × pad`. Work these out when you place shapes next to or below a row or column container.
- `align`: "start" or "center": how row or column children line up across the container. Default `"center"`.
- `pad`: space between the container's edge and its children, 0 to 1000. Default 20. A container also has a 30 px header strip for its label at the top, above the padding.
- `gap`: space between stacked children in a row or column, 0 to 1000. Default 30.

## Connectors (`edges`)

    {"id": "e1", "from": {"node": "users", "side": "auto"}, "to": {"node": "waf", "side": "auto"}, "arrow": "end", "label": "HTTPS"}

- `id` (required): same rules as shape ids, unique among connectors.
- `from`, `to` (required): `node` is the id of a shape (a box or a container); a connector to a shape that doesn't exist is dropped. `side` is "auto", "top", "right", "bottom" or "left". Leave it `"auto"` (the default) and Snapblade picks the sides that face each other. Pin a side only when the meaning needs it.
- `arrow`: "none", "end" or "both". Default `"end"` (an arrowhead at `to`).
- `label`: short text on the line: one to three words, `\n` for a second line. Optional.
- `labelPos`: "start", "center" or "end": where the label sits along the line (`"start"` is the end away from the arrowhead). Omit it to use the diagram's setting.
- `style`: `line` and `dash` only; see Styles. Optional.
- `fixed`: Visio-style glue points, used only when `settings.mode` is `"fixed"`: `{"from": {"side": "right", "frac": 0.5}, "to": {"side": "left", "frac": 0.5}}`, where `side` is "top", "right", "bottom" or "left" and `frac` runs from 0 to 1 along that side. Don't write it otherwise.

## Styles

    "style": {"line": "green", "fill": "pair", "tint": 16, "dash": "dashed"}

Every key is optional.

- `line`: a preset, "slate", "blue", "teal", "green", "amber", "orange", "red" or "violet", which adapts to the light and dark themes; or a fixed color `"#rrggbb"`. Omit it for the theme's default ink.
- `fill` (shapes only): `"pair"` (the default: a light tint of the line color), `"none"` (transparent) or `"#rrggbb"`.
- `tint` (shapes only): strength of the paired tint, 0 to 100. Defaults 16 for boxes and 7 for containers.
- `dash`: "solid", "dashed" or "dotted". Default `"solid"`.

Use color for meaning, one style per kind of thing (for example databases green, caches amber, external services dashed with no fill), and say what each one means in the legend.

## Diagram settings (`settings`)

Usually leave `settings` out.

- `mode`: how connectors attach to a side: "fixed" (Visio-style fixed points), "even" (even spacing) or "straighten" (even spacing, then straighten). Default "straighten".
- `grid`: snap step in px for moving shapes: 5, 10 or 20. Default 10.
- `routing`: connector lines: "ortho" (right angles) or "straight". Default "ortho".
- `radius`: corner radius of connector bends, 0 to 16. Default 6.
- `labelPos`: where connector labels sit unless a connector says otherwise: "start", "center" or "end". Default "start".
- `showSlots`: true or false: mark where connectors attach. Default true.
- `walls`: true or false: keep shapes 20 px apart while the user edits. Default true.
- `autonumber`: true or false: number the messages of a sequence diagram. Default false.
- `footbox`: true or false: draw a sequence diagram's participants at the bottom too. Default true.
- `activation`: true or false: draw a sequence diagram's activation bars (see Sequence diagrams). Default true.

## Title block and legend

    "title": {"show": true, "title": "Order platform", "version": "1.0", "date": "2026-10-07", "author": "", "pos": "bottom-right"}
    "legend": {"show": true, "heading": "Legend", "pos": "bottom-left", "labels": {"box:green||pair": "Database"}, "hidden": []}

- Title block: `show` true draws it. `title` (empty: the file's name), `version`, `date` and `author` are text; empty ones are left out. `pos` is "top-left", "top-right", "bottom-left" or "bottom-right". Default `"bottom-right"`.
- Legend: `show` true draws it, `heading` is its heading (default `"Legend"`), `pos` as above (default `"bottom-left"`). The legend makes its own rows, one per distinct style in use; unstyled shapes and connectors get no row. `labels` maps a row's key to what that style means. `hidden` lists the keys of rows to leave out.
- A row's key is `<kind>:<line>|<dash>|<fill>`. `kind` is `box`, `container` or `connector` (in a sequence diagram `participant`, `message` or `note`). `line` is the preset or hex color, empty if none. `dash` is empty for solid. For shapes, `fill` is `pair` (followed by the tint if one is set, as in `pair30`) when the shape has a line color, empty for the default fill without one, or `none` or the hex color. Connectors have no fill part. Examples: a green box: `box:green||pair`; a container with a blue line and a 30% tint: `container:blue||pair30`; a dashed box with no fill: `box:|dashed|none`; a dashed connector: `connector:|dashed`; an orange dashed connector: `connector:orange|dashed`.
- Both blocks sit just outside the diagram in their corner. You never position them.

## Laying it out well

- Flow left to right in tiers (for example clients, edge, services, data, external), one column per tier. Top to bottom is fine when that reads better.
- Line shapes up so connectors run straight. A connector is straight when the two sides it joins face each other and overlap: Snapblade slides the anchors on the less busy side to line up with the other. So give connected shapes overlapping spans (the same center line is best), and make a box with many connectors on one side tall enough that its partners all face it.
- One diagram can mix directions: a request path left to right with an event fan-out below it is fine.
- Boxes are usually 140 to 160 wide and 50 to 60 tall. Make a box taller (90 to 120) when many connectors meet one of its sides.
- Keep at least 20 px between any two shapes in the same container or on the canvas. Leave 80 to 140 px between columns so connectors have room for bends and labels, and 30 to 60 px between shapes in a column.
- Use `"column"` (or `"row"`) containers for tiers: you only place the container and Snapblade stacks what's inside. Use a `"free"` container when its children need their own positions: place them inside it, at least `pad` from its edges and below its header, and make the container big enough to hold them.
- List containers before the shapes inside them, and list a row's or column's children in the order they should appear.
- Keep ids short and readable (`orders-api`). Keep labels short: a box says what it is; a connector says what flows (`HTTPS`, `SQL`, `/orders`).

## Checklist

- Valid JSON. Every id unique. Every `from.node`, `to.node` and `parent` names an existing shape, and every `parent` is a `"group"`.
- No two shapes overlap or sit closer than 20 px, except a container and the shapes inside it. Opening a file never moves anything, so this is up to you.
- In a sequence diagram: every `from`, `to` and note `on` names a participant in `parts`, ids are unique across participants and rows, each reply comes right after its call, and every frame start has its end below it.
- With tabs: version 2, a `pages` list, and each page's `diagram` follows the rules above.
- Only the fields and values described here.

## Example

The sample diagram that ships with Snapblade:

```json
{
  "format": "snapblade",
  "version": 1,
  "diagram": {
    "nodes": [
      {"id":"users","kind":"box","label":"Customers","x":40,"y":195,"w":120,"h":60,"parent":null,"style":{"line":"blue"}},
      {"id":"edge","kind":"group","label":"Edge","x":220,"y":150,"w":180,"h":270,"parent":null,"layout":"column","align":"center","pad":20,"gap":30},
      {"id":"waf","kind":"box","label":"Web app firewall","x":0,"y":0,"w":140,"h":50,"parent":"edge"},
      {"id":"lb","kind":"box","label":"Load balancer","x":0,"y":0,"w":140,"h":120,"parent":"edge"},
      {"id":"app","kind":"group","label":"Application tier","x":500,"y":90,"w":200,"h":470,"parent":null,"layout":"free","align":"center","pad":20,"gap":30},
      {"id":"orders","kind":"box","label":"Orders API","x":520,"y":140,"w":160,"h":60,"parent":"app"},
      {"id":"inv","kind":"box","label":"Inventory API","x":520,"y":310,"w":160,"h":60,"parent":"app"},
      {"id":"pay","kind":"box","label":"Payments API","x":520,"y":480,"w":160,"h":60,"parent":"app"},
      {"id":"data","kind":"group","label":"Data tier","x":800,"y":90,"w":200,"h":300,"parent":null,"layout":"column","align":"center","pad":20,"gap":20},
      {"id":"odb","kind":"box","label":"Orders DB","x":0,"y":0,"w":160,"h":50,"parent":"data","style":{"line":"green"}},
      {"id":"cache","kind":"box","label":"Redis cache","x":0,"y":0,"w":160,"h":90,"parent":"data","style":{"line":"amber"}},
      {"id":"idb","kind":"box","label":"Inventory DB","x":0,"y":0,"w":160,"h":50,"parent":"data","style":{"line":"green"}},
      {"id":"gw","kind":"box","label":"Payment gateway\n(external)","x":820,"y":480,"w":160,"h":60,"parent":null,"style":{"dash":"dashed","fill":"none"}}
    ],
    "edges": [
      {"id":"e1","from":{"node":"users","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"waf","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end","label":"HTTPS"},
      {"id":"e2","from":{"node":"waf","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"lb","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end"},
      {"id":"e3","from":{"node":"lb","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"orders","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end","label":"/orders"},
      {"id":"e4","from":{"node":"lb","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"inv","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end","label":"/stock"},
      {"id":"e5","from":{"node":"lb","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"pay","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end","label":"/pay"},
      {"id":"e6","from":{"node":"orders","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"odb","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end","label":"SQL"},
      {"id":"e7","from":{"node":"orders","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"cache","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end"},
      {"id":"e8","from":{"node":"inv","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"cache","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end"},
      {"id":"e9","from":{"node":"inv","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"idb","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end","label":"SQL"},
      {"id":"e10","from":{"node":"pay","side":"auto"},"to":{"node":"gw","side":"auto"},"arrow":"end","label":"REST\nmTLS","style":{"dash":"dashed"}}
    ],
    "settings": {"mode":"straighten","grid":10,"showSlots":true,"routing":"ortho","radius":6,"labelPos":"start","walls":true,"autonumber":false,"footbox":true,"activation":true},
    "title": {"show":true,"title":"Order platform","version":"0.3","date":"2026-10-07","author":"","pos":"bottom-right"},
    "legend": {"show":true,"heading":"Legend","pos":"bottom-left","labels":{"box:blue||pair":"People and client apps","box:green||pair":"Database","box:amber||pair":"Cache","box:|dashed|none":"Third-party service","connector:|dashed":"Leaves our network"},"hidden":[]}
  }
}
```

## Sequence diagrams

A sequence diagram is a different kind of file: participants left to right, and rows (messages, notes and frames) top to bottom. Nothing in it has a position. Snapblade makes each column as wide as the labels next to it need and spaces the rows evenly, so you only decide the order.

    {"format": "snapblade", "version": 1, "diagram": {"type": "sequence", "parts": [...], "rows": [...], "settings": {...}, "title": {...}, "legend": {...}}}

- `type` (required): `"sequence"`. Leave out `nodes` and `edges`; a sequence diagram doesn't use them.
- `parts`: the participants, in order from left to right, at most 100: `{"id": "orders", "kind": "participant", "label": "Orders API"}`. `id` follows the shape id rules, `label` is the text (`\n` for a second line), `kind` may be left out, and `style` works as for boxes. `head` is the head's shape, "box", "actor", "database" or "queue": an actor is a stick figure with the name under it, a database a cylinder, a queue a cylinder on its side. Leave it out for a box, the default.
- `rows`: messages, notes and frame lines in the order things happen, at most 1000. Ids are unique across participants and rows.
- A message: `{"id": "m1", "from": "cust", "to": "web", "type": "sync", "label": "Place order"}`. `from` and `to` are participant ids, the same one for a self-message; a message naming a participant that doesn't exist is dropped. `type` is "sync", "async" or "reply": a call that waits for an answer (filled arrowhead), one that doesn't wait (open arrowhead), or the answer (dashed). Default `"sync"`. `style`: `line` and `dash` only; a reply is dashed unless `dash` says otherwise.
- A note: `{"id": "n1", "kind": "note", "side": "right", "on": ["gw"], "label": "Can take up to 5 s"}`. `side` is "left", "right" or "over". `on` lists the participant it sits beside, or for `"over"` one or two participants (the note spans from one to the other). A note takes a row of its own. `style` works as for boxes.
- A frame (alt, opt, loop, par) is rows around the rows it holds: a start `{"id": "f1", "kind": "frame", "type": "alt", "label": "approved"}`, then the rows, then an end `{"id": "f1x", "kind": "end"}`. For an alt or par, an else line `{"id": "f1e", "kind": "else", "label": "declined"}` between them starts the next section. `type` is "alt", "opt", "loop" or "par": one of several paths, only if the condition holds, repeats while it holds, sections run at the same time. Default "alt". `label` is the condition, shown in brackets (leave the brackets out). Frames nest, at most 20 deep. An end with no start, or an else line outside an alt or par, is dropped; a start with no end is closed after the last row. A frame is drawn as wide as the lifelines its rows touch.
- A divider `{"id": "d1", "kind": "divider", "label": "Fulfilment"}` is a row that marks a new phase: a double line across the whole diagram with the label in the middle. A delay `{"id": "d2", "kind": "delay", "label": "5 minutes later"}` is a row that shows time passing: the lifelines go dotted for a stretch. `kind` is "divider" or "delay"; `label` may be empty. Either can sit inside a frame.
- `groups` (optional): boxes around neighbouring participants, like PlantUML's `box ... end box`: `{"id": "platform", "kind": "group", "label": "Our platform", "parts": ["web", "orders", "pay"]}`. `parts` lists participant ids that sit side by side in `parts` order; a participant is in one group at most, and groups don't nest. `style` works as for containers. The ids share the namespace with participants and rows.
- `settings.autonumber` numbers the messages, `settings.footbox` repeats the participants at the bottom, and `settings.activation` (default `true`) draws activation bars. Bars are automatic: a sync call starts one on the participant it calls, and a reply back closes the latest open call between the two (in an alt, each section's reply counts and the bar runs to the last). A call with no reply lasts to that participant's last message before the caller sends again. A caller with no bar of its own gets one for as long as it waits. Async messages start none. So send a reply for every call you want to read as finished. The other settings don't apply. The title block and legend work as above.
- Put each reply right after the call it answers. Keep labels short: an operation, an endpoint or an event name.

The sequence sample that ships with Snapblade:

```json
{
  "format": "snapblade",
  "version": 1,
  "diagram": {
    "type": "sequence",
    "parts": [
      {"id":"cust","kind":"participant","label":"Customer","head":"actor","style":{"line":"blue"}},
      {"id":"web","kind":"participant","label":"Web app"},
      {"id":"orders","kind":"participant","label":"Orders API"},
      {"id":"pay","kind":"participant","label":"Payments API"},
      {"id":"gw","kind":"participant","label":"Payment gateway\n(external)","style":{"dash":"dashed","fill":"none"}},
      {"id":"bus","kind":"participant","label":"Event bus","head":"queue","style":{"line":"amber"}}
    ],
    "rows": [
      {"id":"m1","from":"cust","to":"web","type":"sync","label":"Place order"},
      {"id":"m2","from":"web","to":"orders","type":"sync","label":"POST /orders"},
      {"id":"m3","from":"orders","to":"orders","type":"sync","label":"Validate cart"},
      {"id":"m4","from":"orders","to":"pay","type":"sync","label":"Authorize payment"},
      {"id":"m5","from":"pay","to":"gw","type":"sync","label":"Charge card"},
      {"id":"n1","kind":"note","side":"over","on":["pay","gw"],"label":"mTLS. Can take up to 5 s."},
      {"id":"m6","from":"gw","to":"pay","type":"reply","label":"Result"},
      {"id":"f1","kind":"frame","type":"alt","label":"approved"},
      {"id":"m7","from":"pay","to":"orders","type":"reply","label":"Authorized"},
      {"id":"m8","from":"orders","to":"bus","type":"async","label":"OrderPlaced"},
      {"id":"m9","from":"orders","to":"web","type":"reply","label":"201 Created"},
      {"id":"m10","from":"web","to":"cust","type":"reply","label":"Order confirmed"},
      {"id":"f1e","kind":"else","label":"declined"},
      {"id":"m11","from":"pay","to":"orders","type":"reply","label":"Declined"},
      {"id":"m12","from":"orders","to":"web","type":"reply","label":"402 Payment required"},
      {"id":"m13","from":"web","to":"cust","type":"reply","label":"Show payment error"},
      {"id":"f1x","kind":"end"}
    ],
    "groups": [
      {"id":"platform","kind":"group","label":"Our platform","parts":["web","orders","pay"]}
    ],
    "settings": {"mode":"straighten","grid":10,"showSlots":true,"routing":"ortho","radius":6,"labelPos":"start","walls":true,"autonumber":false,"footbox":true,"activation":true},
    "title": {"show":true,"title":"Checkout","version":"0.3","date":"2026-10-07","author":"","pos":"bottom-right"},
    "legend": {"show":true,"heading":"Legend","pos":"bottom-left","labels":{"participant:blue||pair":"People","participant:|dashed|none":"Third-party service","participant:amber||pair":"Messaging"},"hidden":[]}
  }
}
```

## Several diagrams in one file (tabs)

A file can hold several diagrams, each shown as a tab: for example an architecture diagram and the sequence diagrams that go with it. Use version 2 and a `pages` list instead of `diagram`:

    {"format": "snapblade", "version": 2, "active": 0, "pages": [{"name": "Architecture", "diagram": {...}}, {"name": "Checkout", "diagram": {"type": "sequence", ...}}]}

- `pages`: the tabs in order, at most 50. Each has a `name` (text, up to 100 characters; empty gets a default) and a `diagram` written exactly as above. Ids only need to be unique within their own diagram.
- `active`: the index of the tab the file opens at. Default 0.
